statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-95184: GnuTLS does not enforce a permittedSubtrees name constraint of the directoryName form, so a leaf whose subject is outside the permitted subtree (EE O=Evil under a CA permitted only O=Good) is accepted (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-95184, proof of concept https://github.com/lkloliver/poc/tree/main/CVE-2026-95184). The GnuTLS maintainers dispute the CVE because exploiting it needs a certificate issued by a CA the user already trusts (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/work_items/1965), and Debian lists gnutls28 in trixie as unfixed with urgency unimportant (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-95184, Debian bug 1150522). Upstream changed this behaviour in GnuTLS 3.8.14 anyway: permitted constraints of a type GnuTLS does not match now cause rejection, and a non-empty subject counts as a name for a directoryName constraint (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/988f435abdd33c66c75ca2069118e9f1c7fb0206 and https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/5d1d734f596d89842c7134d5b43c25f45f0306ec, which build on https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/6e11fea0d5c5886bd215b81fb35baf10b031c8d8 and https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/261c718f998351e71db3590a8df78b15961e7e26; GnuTLS 3.8.14 NEWS, 'Count subject as name for DN constraint validation' and 'Reject on unsupported permitted name constraint types'). The DHI Debian repository publishes two builds of this owner for Debian 13, both made from Debian's 3.8.9-3+deb13u4. The newer build carries a backport of those four commits adapted to GnuTLS 3.8.9: a directoryName constraint, permitted or excluded, rejects any leaf with a non-empty subject, because GnuTLS 3.8.9 does not match DNs against the constraint. This fails closed, so it also rejects some chains that a DN comparison would accept. We checked both builds on amd64 and arm64, each package verified against the repository index checksum, using the symbol tables in their -dbgsym packages: in the newer build, the internal check_unsupported_constraint function of lib/x509/name_constraints.c reads the permitted constraints as well as the excluded ones (it calls gnutls_x509_name_constraints_get_permitted), both in libgnutls.so.30 (libgnutls30t64) and in the static libgnutls.a (libgnutls28-dev); in the older build it reads only the excluded constraints, as GnuTLS 3.8.9 does. The changelog shipped in the newer build's packages lists the backport for this CVE. The range ends at the newer build. The older build, and builds made from Debian's earlier 3.8.9-3+deb13u2 and 3.8.9-3+deb13u3 sources, do not have the change and sort below it, so they are reported as affected.
